answer.rationale: p99 latency is climbing 5x on a write path that just took a release 2 hours ago, during peak settlement traffic. Two inherited memories are directly relevant and worth verifying before committing: memory_b1 (rollback cleared a prior checkout error spike cleanly, no customer impact) and memory_b6 (staged release gating caught bad builds fast, canary surfaced regressions inside an hour). Together they support the working hypothesis that this build is the regression and that rollback is a known-clean lever. I am not choosing regional_failover (memory_b2) because a release-correlated latency climb on the write path is more consistent with a bad build than with regional degradation, and failover during peak settlement would risk losing or duplicating in-flight customer writes, violating the primary objective. I am not adding capacity because memory_b5 showed the bottleneck was routing/load pattern, not raw capacity, and provisioning headroom (memory_b3) is about pre-peak scaling, not live mid-incident remediation. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) would shed load and drop customer writes, also violating the objective. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) does not address a write-path regression. Rollback is the single highest-confidence, customer-write-preserving intervention, and the two memories I am verifying both reduce the residual uncertainty about whether rollback will complete cleanly and whether the regression is build-borne.
